strategyPosture: Stay in the screened-research posture the pullback screen already sets: the dislocations are sentiment-driven with fundamentals intact (AVGO +55% revenue at -31.6% from high; VRT +27.7% at -45.2%), so build the entry list and verify theses — but with the 10Y at 5.08% and the FOMC on Oct 27-28, stage entries rather than sizing into a still-falling tape.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree this is rotation rather than a confirmed broad rollover, but the calm is narrower than the headline index suggests: leadership is churning underneath a flat SPY, and the read flips if credit conditions flip. Treat index-level flatness as a weak signal, not an all-clear.
themes.dataAnchor: The concentration read is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER: the Mag7 average sits -10.61% from its 52-week high against SPY's -1.5%, a -9.11-point divergence gap, with TSLA weakest at -27.8% and AAPL strongest at -1.7%. Credit does not confirm a rollover: SLOOS lending standards are LOOSE at 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold, and HY OAS is 3.25%. Small caps tell the same rotation story — IWM is -7.52% over 3 months while SPY is +1.98%.
themes.label: Leadership Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The index looks calm — SPY at 769.75, +0.02% on the day and only -1.5% from its 52-week high — which the market is reading as nothing being wrong.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS tightening off 0% or HY OAS widening through 3.75% would convert rotation into rollover; a Mag7-vs-SPY divergence gap narrowing back inside -5 points would confirm healthy broadening.

themes.counterRead: This is the clearest data-ahead-of-price setup in the book: the businesses are compounding while the multiples compress. The honest caution is timing, not thesis — VRT is still making lower lows today (worst laggard at -12.62% 1m), so the dislocation is an opportunity set to stage into, not a bottom already confirmed.
themes.dataAnchor: AVGO is the top-conviction name (score 81, tier A): revenue growing +55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin, $26,914M FCF at a 42.1% margin — while the stock sits -31.6% from its 52-week high at RSI 38.9. VRT shows the same pattern deeper: revenue +27.7% YoY and $1,894M FCF against a price -45.2% from its high, RSI 28.1, and a -12.62% one-month slide. Semicap names (LRCX, AMAT, KLAC) cluster at RSI 32-35 with declines classified as multiple compression, not thesis breaks.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure: Fundamentals Ahead of Price
themes.narrative: The tape is pricing an AI-infrastructure fade: the dislocation screen is dominated by AI suppliers marked SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, and Vertiv fell another -6.12% today.
themes.watchFor: VRT holding above today's low with RSI recovering through 35, or AVGO reclaiming momentum after its next earnings print, would mark the dislocation closing; another -5% leg in VRT on no fundamental news extends the entry window rather than invalidating it.

themes.counterRead: The story ran ahead of any deliverable fundamentals in the SMR/OKLO complex — that leg is narrative-ahead and still deflating. VST is the opposite shape (cash generation priced at a discount), but the deteriorating revenue-inflection flag means even the quality name gets verified before sizing, not bought on the theme.
themes.dataAnchor: SMR is -28.92% over one month, OKLO -18.16%, and URA -13.66% — the pre-revenue nuclear complex is the tape's worst cluster. Vistra breaks the pattern: VST is +8.63% over one month, insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, revenue is growing +19.1% with $1,318M FCF at a 2.9x P/S — yet it still sits -29.7% from its high, and its watchlist promotion flags revenue inflection as DETERIORATING.
themes.label: Speculative Nuclear Unwind vs Cash-Generative Power
themes.narrative: The nuclear/AI-power trade was priced as a straight line up; the speculative end is now unwinding hard while the market still talks about the theme as one block.
themes.watchFor: SMR or OKLO posting a second consecutive positive week would signal the speculative unwind exhausting; for VST, a revenue-inflection upgrade from DETERIORATING on the next print is the promotion trigger.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree on the setup: a restrictive curve with no credit crack yet, 12 days before the Oct 27-28 FOMC (also flagged HIGH signal). The hike-fear headlines are running ahead of any credit evidence — positioning should key off spreads and the FOMC, not off the CPI headline flow.
themes.dataAnchor: The rates stack is genuinely restrictive: 2Y at 4.79%, 10Y at 5.08%, 30Y at 5.42%, real 10Y at 2.73%, curve 2s10s at +0.29. But the stress gauges refuse to confirm: HY OAS is 3.25%, SLOOS is LOOSE at 0%, SPY closed the day +0.02%, and even the VIX bid (+10.28% today) only takes it to 16.84. QQQ's -0.67% day against +2.75% one-month performance is a hedge bid, not a break.
themes.label: Hot CPI, Unbroken Credit
themes.narrative: The September CPI event is active with HIGH signal strength, and the headline flow is rate-hike fear — chipmakers sinking on inflation data, hike odds climbing.
themes.watchFor: A 10Y close above 5.2% or HY OAS widening past 3.75% before the Oct 28 FOMC would break the calm-credit read; a VIX close above 20 would confirm hedging has become liquidation.

themes.counterRead: Crypto leadership while the 10Y sits at 5.08% and small caps are -7.52% over three months is a narrow, speculative bid, not broad risk-on confirmation. BMNR in the book rides this complex; the move is tradeable momentum, not a thesis upgrade, and leveraged torque (CONL) decays fastest if the bid stalls.
themes.dataAnchor: CONL leads all tracked names at +15.83% over one month and +8.71% today; COIN is +9.98% on the month and +4.65% today; IBIT is +8.05% on the month. No fundamental data point in this input — no revenue, spread, or insider signal — anchors the move; it is price-only momentum, and the leaderboard's top slot is a leveraged vehicle, which is the signature of narrative running ahead of evidence.
themes.label: Crypto Torque Leading the Leaderboard
themes.narrative: The one-month leaderboard is topped by crypto torque: the market is expressing its risk appetite through leveraged crypto exposure first.
themes.watchFor: COIN failing to hold its one-month gains on a down day for IBIT, or CONL underperforming COIN over a full week, would signal the torque bid exhausting; broadening of 1-month leadership beyond crypto names would be the healthier read.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move most likely materializes in AI-infrastructure suppliers where revenue growth and price have diverged widest — AVGO (tier A, score 81) and VRT (RSI 28.1) — triggered by either name stabilizing after earnings confirmation, while speculative nuclear (SMR -28.92% 1m) continues to deflate in the background.
